labels: Six pairs of electrons from six F- ions
note: text_layer null; read from the image. No 'Fig. 5.x' caption line is printed for this in-text orbital box diagram, so `caption` is left empty rather than invented. Labels are read row by row: each row's left-hand label first, then the labels printed under its box sets from left to right. PRINTED AS SHOWN, apparently a misprint in the book: the hybrid set in the middle row is labelled 'sp3d3 hybrid' (s p superscript 3, d superscript 3) although the row's own left label says 'sp3d2 hybridised orbitals of Co3+' and the text above calls it sp3d2; both were re-checked at high zoom and the superscript on the hybrid label is unmistakably a 3. It is copied as printed, not corrected. Wrapped labels are joined with single spaces: 'sp3d2 hybridised' / 'orbitals of Co3+', '[CoF6]3-' / '(outer orbital or' / ' high spin complex)', and 'Six pairs of electrons' / 'from six F- ions'. 'Orbitals of Co3+ion' is printed with no space between the superscript 3+ and 'ion' and is copied as printed. Notation: superscripts and subscripts are flattened to plain characters (Co superscript 3+ -> 'Co3+'; [CoF6] with subscript 6 and superscript 3- -> '[CoF6]3-'; F superscript minus -> 'F-'); the printed superscript minus is written as a plain hyphen-minus. Known structural loss: the electron occupancies are DRAWN as up/down arrows in ruled boxes and cannot be carried in a flat label list. For the record, all three rows show 3d as five boxes with the first pair-filled and four singly occupied; row 1 also has an empty 4s box, three empty 4p boxes and five empty 4d boxes; row 2 has six empty hybrid boxes and three empty 4d boxes; row 3 has six pair-filled hybrid boxes and three empty 4d boxes. Over-included by the crop and excluded as belonging to other blocks: the paragraph above ('hybrid orbitals. Thus, the complex has octahedral geometry and is diamagnetic because of the absence of unpaired electron. In the formation of this complex, since the inner d orbital (3d) is used in hybridisation, the complex, [Co(NH3)6]3+ is called an inner orbital or low spin or spin paired complex. The paramagnetic octahedral complex, [CoF6]3- uses outer orbital (4d) in hybridisation (sp3d2). It is thus called outer orbital or high spin or spin free complex. Thus:') and, below the box, the start of the next diagram's boxes with the text 'In tetrahedral complexes one s and three p orbitals...'. The crop is clipped at the RIGHT edge, cutting the right end of the row-1 4d box set; the printed labels are all complete. A faint diagonal 'NCERT / not to be republished' watermark crosses the figure without obscuring it.
